digest.component_or_area: source code comments and docstrings quality enforcement
propositions: Source code comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run IDs, and dated incident narratives that decay over time due to rebasing, retention policies, and historical drift.

A detector must identify rot-prone patterns: SHA-like hex strings (7+ alphanumeric chars), run/job/thread IDs (8+ digits), and date tokens paired with past-tense incident verbs (failed, broke, regressed, fixed, caught, observed, hit, crashed, flaked).

Detected violations are remediated by replacing rot-prone refs with durable forms: ticket/epic/story/bug citations, behavioral descriptions searchable via git log, or 'context: external' escape hatches for vendor-pinned refs.

A CI guard (check_comment_hygiene.py) must be wired into the build-and-test workflow to block reintroduction of rot-prone refs in comments and docstrings, with self-exclusion for the detector's own unit-test fixtures.
The word-triple-alias acceptor pattern must not match hyphenated filenames or path components; only sentence-final aliases are valid, to prevent false accepts like 'sync-hardening-proposal.md'.
All detector-hit sites across the tree must be remediated with zero in-tree escape-hatch suppressions, and the post-fix tree must scan clean.
